original_value: Label distribution learning (LDL) is a novel multi-label learning paradigm proposed in recent years for solving label ambiguity. Existing approaches typically exploit label correlations globally to improve the effectiveness of label distribution learning, by assuming that the label correlations are shared by all instances. However, different instances may share different label correlations, and few correlations are globally applicable in real-world applications. In this paper, we propose a new label distribution learning algorithm by exploiting sample correlations locally (LDL-SCL). To encode the influence of local samples, we design a local correlation vector for each instance based on the clustered local samples.  Then we predict the label distribution for an unseen instance based on the original features and the local correlation vector simultaneously. Experimental results demonstrate that LDL-SCL can effectively deal with the label distribution problems and perform remarkably better than the state-of-the-art LDL methods.

result.paraphrase: Label distribution learning (LDL) is a recently proposed multi-label learning paradigm for addressing label ambiguity. Current methods usually use global label correlations to enhance label distribution learning, based on the assumption that the same correlations apply to every instance. In practice, however, different instances can share different label correlations, and only a few are globally valid. This paper introduces a new LDL algorithm, LDL-SCL, which exploits sample correlations locally. To represent the impact of local samples, we construct a local correlation vector for each instance from clustered local samples. We then estimate the label distribution of an unseen instance using both the original features and the local correlation vector. Experimental results show that LDL-SCL can effectively handle label distribution problems and performs significantly better than state-of-the-art LDL methods.
